verdicts.corrected_statement:
At tree level, exchange of a spin-J field between spinless point sources has a pole residue that is a degree-J polynomial in gamma = u1.u2: P_J(gamma) if massive, T_J(gamma) if massless. The (v/c)^2 coefficients are J(J+1)/4 and J^2/2 [D, verified]. Every such residue increases with v, so no single spin gives a gate.
Massless J >= 3 particles have no couplings that survive at low energy (Weinberg 1964 [S]; Porrati 2008 [S]). A finite number of light massive J > 2 particles cannot couple causally to gravitons (Afkhami-Jeddi-Kundu-Tajdini 2019 [S]).
Hence, for local Lorentz-invariant exchange of finitely many finite-spin fields, the long-range force between ordinary bodies has a tree-level residue A + B gamma + C gamma^2, times spin-independent kinematic factors, plus post-Minkowskian loop terms whose velocity scale is c. The velocity dependence is O(v^2/c^2) unless tuned.
The tuned J=0/J=1 residual turns repulsive above its zero (-468 times the static residual at 2600 km/s when the zero is at 120 km/s). For ordinary bodies it also violates the equivalence principle at eta ~ 1e4.
Exceptions lie outside these assumptions: infinite towers (T4), continuous-spin carriers (T9), non-locality (T5), preferred frames (T6, T7).

verdicts.reason:
The critic's sentence 'no macroscopic fields from massless spin >= 3' matches the abstract's own words, which I retrieved [S].
What the theorem proves (precise form per Bekaert-Boulanger-Sundell, RMP 84, 987 (2012), arXiv:1007.0435 [S]): soft emission of a massless spin-s particle, with Lorentz invariance, imposes a conservation law of order s-1 on the external momenta, sum_n g_n p_n^{mu1}...p_n^{mu(s-1)} = 0. For s > 2 there is no generic solution, so 'all coupling constants must be equal to zero'. Massless higher spins 'may exist, but they cannot have couplings that survive in the limit of low energy' and 'cannot mediate long-range interactions'. Trivial (permutation) scattering is exempt.
Assumptions: flat spacetime; an S-matrix with massless finite-helicity particles; Lorentz invariance; soft emission controlled by cubic couplings; generic kinematics.
Later results:
- Weinberg-Witten, PLB 96, 59 (1980) [S]: in theories with a Lorentz-covariant stress tensor, massless j > 1 particles (composite or elementary) are forbidden; with a covariant conserved current, charged j > 1/2 particles are forbidden. This excludes composite or emergent higher-spin carriers, not GR itself.
- Porrati, PRD 78, 065016 (2008) [S]: massless particles interacting with gravity in Minkowski space can have at most spin two. This strengthens the result.
- Coleman-Mandula (per BBS [S]): no higher-spin conserved charges, given finitely many species below any mass and generically non-vanishing amplitudes.
- AKT 2019 [S]: extends the conclusion to finitely many massive J > 2 particles. The exception is an infinite fine-tuned tower, which affects graviton dynamics at its lightest mass.
Outside the assumptions: AdS (Vasiliev; no S-matrix) and continuous-spin representations. Schuster-Toro-Zhou 2023 [S] conjecture CSPs 'may in fact mediate known long-range forces'.
Corrections:
(a) The gap headline 'only J <= 2 can be long-range (Weinberg 1964)', and Q2's 'of degree <= 2 for long range (Weinberg 1964 [S])', extend the theorem to massive fields, which it does not cover.
(b) The critic's [S] rested on search summaries. The abstract is now [S] from the publisher's page; the full text is still unread.

Weinberg, Phys. Rev. 135, B1049 (1964) [S: APS abstract; full text not read]. From Lorentz invariance and the S-matrix pole structure, the soft-emission amplitude of a massless integer-spin particle must satisfy mass-shell gauge invariance. For spin >= 3 this forces every coupling that survives at low energy to vanish, hence 'no macroscopic fields corresponding to particles of spin 3 or higher'. new_claims.statement:
Non-minimal or derivative couplings of spinless point sources cannot gate a long-range force.
- At a light pole the residue is built from contractions of the carrier's J indices with u1 and u2.
- Extra derivatives bring factors (u_i.q), which vanish in the classical limit (q.u_i = O(q^2/m)), or powers of q^2, which cancel the pole and leave contact or shorter-range terms.
- Couplings to a body's own momentum add only powers of p_i.p_j = m_i m_j gamma, so the residue stays a polynomial of bounded degree.
- On shell, a three-point vertex chi(p1) -> chi(p3) + carrier depends only on t = (p1 - p3)^2, whatever its form, local or not. So no vertex can depend on the other body's momentum.

- For the scalar spatial current, their eq. (129) gives, to leading order, L_int ~ (g^2/4 pi r)[1 - (rho^2 r^2/32)(|v_ij| - v_ij.rhat)^2 + ...]. The correction depends only on relative velocity, vanishes for co-moving pairs and for motion along the separation, and is 'important at long distances, rho v r ~ 1'.
- Static potentials are standard for homogeneous currents but deviate at rho r ~ 1 for inhomogeneous ones.
- This is the one framework found in which a long-range force acquires a relative-velocity-dependent perturbation at v << c, the shape of Paul's question. But its threshold is distance-dependent, v ~ c (hbar c/rho r), not a fixed v*. A 120 km/s threshold at 1 kpc needs rho = 1.6e-23 eV (then hbar c/rho = 0.40 pc); at 10 kpc, 1.6e-24 eV. - The paper gives no velocity-dependent result for vector-like currents. It says a graviton-CSP needs a non-Abelian theory with tensor correspondence that is not yet developed. Its rough photon bounds are rho_gamma <~ 1e-6 eV, and ~1e-9 eV from stellar cooling.
- The record contains no CSP.

overall:
All four critic claims hold in substance, and each needs a scope, wording or citation correction. The critic missed one real loophole: continuous-spin carriers (T9).

c1 (corrected). My own derivation reproduces P_J (massive) and T_J (massless), the coefficients J(J+1)/4 and J^2/2, the spins J = 4996 and 3533, and the tuned-pair numbers (1.2483e7; -468.47 at 2600 km/s). It used explicit Lorentzian traceless projections, the Fierz-Pauli and de Donder anchors, and a helicity sum. Corrections:
- the polynomial is the tree-level residue; loops add terms whose only velocity scale is c;
- Weinberg covers massless spins only; light massive J > 2 needs AKT 2019 [S], which allows an infinite tower;
- J ~ c/v* buys an O(1) increase, never a gate;
- the tuned pair also violates the equivalence principle (eta ~ 1e4).

c1-weinberg (corrected). The APS abstract, retrieved [S], says 'no macroscopic fields corresponding to particles of spin 3 or higher'. The precise content (a conservation law of order s-1; couplings that survive at low energy must vanish for s > 2; flat space) comes from the Bekaert-Boulanger-Sundell review [S]. Porrati 2008 and Weinberg-Witten 1980 strengthen it [S]; AKT extends it to massive fields; AdS and continuous spin lie outside it.

c2 (corrected). The numbers reproduce (Sun-Earth 2.93e-22; gamma~ - 1 = 4.3e-44; mixed block 2.9e-26). But #13 sec. 5 makes free fall dual rest, which gives zero for gravitating pairs and contradicts #13 sec. 2. The mixed-block term is a power ratio vF/(c^5/G), so it depends on velocity too. The neutron-star anchor is circular.

c6D (corrected). The canonical map is exact. 'Exerts no force' holds in any potential; only 'cannot change relative momenta' is limited to free space or a uniform field (harmonic: 2.56, quartic: 1.63 change). '#13 sec. 5's x^2/2m~' is a misattribution.

Loopholes T1-T8. Derivative couplings, form factors, loops, non-locality and tau with the other moduli give no gate. A spin tower can build only gates that are entire in gamma, with terms ~10^5421169 times the net at v* = 120 km/s; rational gates are impossible. A medium or slow mediator gives preferred-frame dependence: between co-moving bodies the side-by-side force is 1/sqrt(1-V^2/c_s^2) times static, and zero above c_s.

T9, missed. Continuous-spin exchange gives a relative-velocity correction that vanishes for co-moving pairs: Paul's shape. But its threshold scales as 1/r (rho = 1.6e-23 eV for 120 km/s at 1 kpc), no gravitational version exists, and the record has none.

Gate-range. In the non-relativistic operator the fiber-overlap gate is not confined to contact range. The Gaussian symbol is exactly F(k) times V smoothed over hbar/mu = 1.0e-11 m; quantum equals classical-gated to 1e-5 out to 1000 hbar/mu. What makes the record's gate contact-range is X's mass. A light version cannot exist with finitely many local fields: it needs a fiber-resolving infinite tower, excluded by the record's own multi-graviton argument plus Weinberg and Porrati, and its coupling would be decorative.

A related missed issue: a single spin-2 X_mu-nu(x) with any on-shell vertices gives amplitudes polynomial in s, so #11 sec. 8's mechanism needs an unconstructed fiber-resolving X (#11 sec. 14 item 4). #6's 'rational gates' would knee sigma_T without gating the mean field, which strengthens the obituary.

Net for Claude: the obituary's scope (the contact gate) stands. Paul's long-range relative-velocity perturbation of gravity has no carrier within local finite-spin QFT. The only known theoretical shape that gives it (continuous spin) has a distance-dependent threshold and no gravitational theory. The repository was not modified.
